what: A lane that took over another lane's files inherited its ready list (/tmp/round2/ready/records.txt) without knowing: while it was mid-write the runner snapshotted `crates/hir-def/src/deps.rs` with `pub mod awaited;` and no `deps/awaited.rs`, and a commit had to be reverted. Later the same lane edited listed files to call a function in a file not yet listed (hir-ty `frozen::serve`), a second window of the same kind.
whys: The runner builds whatever paths a ready file lists, at the moment it looks.
A ready file says 'these paths are whole' forever, not 'these paths were whole at this content'.
A lane that starts editing a listed file has to remember to remove a file in /tmp, by hand, before its first edit; a successor lane does not know the file exists.
Nothing ties the declaration to the bytes declared: no content hash, no check that every `mod` line of a listed file resolves to a listed or committed file.
The hand-off between lanes is a message, and the state it needs (which files are declared whole, under which name) lives outside the tree.
class: A declaration of readiness that outlives the content it was made about.
prevention: The ready list names each path with its content hash (`shasum` at the time of declaring); the runner takes a path only when the hash still matches and reports the ones that moved to the lane. A python check before each snapshot that every `mod x;` of a taken file resolves to a file that is committed or taken. A lane brief for a successor names the predecessor's ready file.
where: /tmp/round2/ready/<lane>.txt and the round runner's snapshot; crates/hir-def/src/deps.rs
cause: A ready file lists paths, not contents, and a successor lane was not told its predecessor's list was still live.
cost: one reverted commit and one build round
workaround: Remove the ready file before the first edit of any listed file; write it again when the piece is whole.
